context.title: Hezekiah's Prayer Answered
context.summary: Hezekiah goes into the temple and spreads Sennacherib's threatening letter before the Lord. Isaiah brings God's answer, that the king of Assyria will go home the way he came, and that night the angel of the Lord strikes the Assyrian camp.
context.background: Tirhakah (v. 9) was a Cushite ruler of Egypt, perhaps still a prince at the time, whose army marched against Assyria. Sennacherib returned to Nineveh and in 681 BC was murdered by his sons, as verse 38 reports; Babylonian and Assyrian records also mention his murder and the succession of Esarhaddon.

customs.note: Assyrian art shows captives led by cords fastened to rings or hooks through the lips or nose. God will treat the Assyrian king as he treated others.

watchFor: Hezekiah's prayer: 'that all the kingdoms of the earth may know' (v. 20).
A three-year sign of returning harvests (v. 30).
'For mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake' (v. 35).

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: Son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1; 2 Chr. 29:1), whom he succeeded on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. He reigned twenty-nine years (B.C. 726-697).

people.name: Isaiah
people.summary: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

people.name: Amoz
people.summary: Strong, the father of the prophet Isaiah (2 Kings 19:2, 20; 20:1; Isa. 1:1; 2:1). As to his personal history little is positively known.

people.name: Eliakim
people.summary: The son of Hilkiah, who was sent to receive the message of the invading Assyrians and report it to Isaiah (2 Kings 18:18; 19:2; Isa. 36:3; 37:2).

people.name: Shebna
people.summary: Tender youth, “treasurer” over the house in the reign of Hezekiah, i.e., comptroller or governor of the palace. On account of his pride he was ejected from his office, and Eliakim was promoted to it (Isa. 22:15-25).

people.name: Rabshakeh
people.summary: Chief of the princes, the name given to the chief cup-bearer or the vizier of the Assyrian court; one of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah.

people.name: Tirhakah
people.summary: The last king of Egypt of the Ethiopian (the fifteenth) dynasty. He was the brother-in-law of So. He probably ascended the throne about B.C. 692, having been previously king of Ethiopia (2 Kings 19:9; Isa. 37:9), which with Egypt now formed one nation.

people.name: Sennacherib
people.summary: Sin (the god) sends many brothers, son of Sargon, whom he succeeded on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 705), in the 23rd year of Hezekiah. “Like the Persian Xerxes, he was weak and vainglorious, cowardly under reverse, and cruel and boastful in success.”

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Adrammelech
people.summary: A son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria (2 Kings 19:37; Isa. 37:38).

people.name: Sharezer
people.summary: (god) protect the king!, a son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria.

places.name: Assyria
places.summary: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom.

places.name: Lachish
places.summary: Impregnable, a royal Canaanitish city in the Shephelah, or maritime plain of Palestine (Josh. 10:3, 5; 12:11). It was taken and destroyed by the Israelites (Josh. 10:31-33).

places.name: Libnah
places.summary: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites taken by Joshua (Josh. 10:29-32; 12:15). It became one of the Levitical towns in the tribe of Judah (21:13), and was strongly fortified.

places.name: Cush
places.summary: A son, probably the eldest, of Ham, and the father of Nimrod (Gen. 10:8; 1 Chr. 1:10). From him the land of Cush seems to have derived its name.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Eden
places.summary: The garden in which our first parents dewlt (Gen. 2:8-17). No geographical question has been so much discussed as that bearing on its site. It has been placed in Armenia, in the region west of the Caspian Sea, in Media, near Damascus, in Palestine, in Southern Arabia, and in Babylonia.

places.name: Gozan
places.summary: A region in Central Asia to which the Israelites were carried away captive (2 Kings 17:6; 1 Chr. 5:26; 2 Kings 19:12; Isa. 37:12). It was situated in Mesopotamia, on the river Habor (2 Kings 17:6; 18:11), the Khabur, a tributary of the Euphrates.

places.name: Haran
places.summary: Heb. haran, i.e., “parched;” or probably from the Accadian charana, meaning “a road.” A celebrated city of Western Asia, now Harran, where Abram remained, after he left Ur of the Chaldees, till his father Terah died (Gen. 11:31, 32), when he continued his journey into the land of Canaan.

places.name: Rezeph
places.summary: Solid; a stone, (2 Kings 19:12; Isa. 37:12), a fortress near Haran, probably on the west of the Euphrates, conquered by Sennacherib.

places.name: Telassar
places.summary: Or Thelasar, (Isa. 37:12; 2 Kings 19:12), a province in the south-east of Assyria, probably in Babylonia.

places.name: Arpad
places.summary: (Isa. 10:9; 36:19; 37:13), also Arphad, support, a Syrian city near Hamath, along with which it is invariably mentioned (2 Kings 19:13; 18:34; Isa. 10:9), and Damascus (Jer. 49:23).

places.name: Hamath
places.summary: Fortress, the capital of one of the kingdoms of Upper Syria of the same name, on the Orontes, in the valley of Lebanon, at the northern boundary of Palestine (Num. 13:21; 34:8), at the foot of Hermon (Josh. 13:5) towards Damascus (Zech. 9:2; Jer. 49:23).

places.name: Hena
places.summary: One of the cities of Mesopotamia destroyed by sennacherib (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13).

places.name: Ivvah
places.summary: Overturning, a city of the Assyrians, whence colonists were brought to Samaria (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13).

places.name: Sepharvaim
places.summary: Taken by Sargon, king of Assyria (2 Kings 17:24; 18:34; 19:13; Isa. 37:13). It was a double city, and received the common name Sepharvaim, i.e., “the two Sipparas,” or “the two booktowns.”

places.name: Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

places.name: Lebanon
places.summary: White, “the white mountain of Syria,” is the loftiest and most celebrated mountain range in Syria. It is a branch running southward from the Caucasus, and at its lower end forking into two parallel ranges, the eastern or Anti-Lebanon, and the western or Lebanon proper.

places.name: mount Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

places.name: Nineveh
places.summary: First mentioned in Gen. 10:11, which is rendered in the Revised Version, “He [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria and builded Nineveh.” It is not again noticed till the days of Jonah, when it is described (Jonah 3:3; 4:11) as a great and populous city, the flourishing capital of the Assyrian empire (2 Kings 19:36; Isa. 37:37).

events.title: Prophecies of Isaiah
events.summary: Passage: Isaiah 1:1–66:24. People: Isaiah. Lasted about 62 years.
